items.title: I wrapped the Zorks with an LLM
items.raw_excerpt: I grew up on the Infocom games and when microsoft actually open-sourced Zork 1/2/3 I really wanted to figure out how to use LLMs to let you type whatever you want, I always found the amount language that the games "understood" to be so limiting - even if it was pretty state of the art at the time. So I figured out how to wrap it with Tambo.. (and run the game engine in the browser) basically whatever you type gets "translated" into zork-speak and passed to the game - and then the LLM takes the game's output and optionally adds flavor. (the little ">_" button at the top exposes the actual game input) What was a big surprise to me is multi-turn instructions - you can ask it to "Explore all the rooms in the house until you can't find any more" and it will plug away at the game for 10+ "turns"

title_i18n.en: I wrapped the Zorks with an LLM
title_i18n.zh: 我用LLM包装了Zorks。
title_i18n.es: Envolví a los Zorks con un modelo de lenguaje grande.

So I figured out how to wrap it with Tambo.. (and run the game engine in the browser) basically whatever you type gets "translated" into zork-speak and passed to the game - and then the LLM takes the game's output and optionally adds flavor. (the little ">_" button at the top exposes the actual game input) What was a big surprise to me is multi-turn instructions - you can ask it to "Explore all the rooms in the house until you can't find any more" and it will plug away at the game for 10+ "turns"
excerpt_i18n.zh: 我从小玩Infocom游戏长大，当微软开源Zork 1/2/3时，我特别想研究如何用大语言模型实现自由输入——那些游戏能“理解”的语言范围总让我觉得受限。
excerpt_i18n.es: Crecí con los juegos de Infocom y cuando Microsoft liberó el código de Zork 1/2/3 realmente quería descubrir cómo usar modelos de lenguaje grandes para permitirte escribir lo que quieras, siempre me sorprendió la cantidad de lenguaje que los juegos "entendían".

- Paraphrases in ways that change meaning

- Re-read transcripts or scrub audio
- Takes 20-30 minutes per post
- Zero tolerance for publishing errors Camp B: "I trust AI and publish"
- "Good enough" for social media
- Errors are rare enough to accept

As artificial intelligence transitions from conversation to real-life applications, human society stands at a new crossroads. On January 27, 2026, the Tencent Tech for Good Innovation Festival (2026), hosted by Tencent Research Institute, was held in Shenzhen. Under the theme "Happening Now," this year's festival brought together 53 experts, scholars, industry leaders, and practitioners from fields such as global technology, humanities, arts, and education to explore the profound changes occurring in individual lives, industrial forms, and social structures amid the rapid evolution of AI.

In the opening address, Guo Kaitian, Senior Vice President of Tencent Group and Chairman of Tencent Research Institute, stated that artificial intelligence represents a profound transformation on a century-long scale, which must be approached with the patience of long-termism, advanced with confidence in universal capability empowerment, and guided by a goodwill toward society. He emphasized that AI is not a tool for short-term competition but a marathon requiring sustained investment and co-creation with users and society. Its value lies not in replacing humans but in amplifying human potential and helping more ordinary people gain capabilities and opportunities. Guo Kaitian also stressed that tech companies must pay close attention to groups with weaker adaptability and limited resources during the accelerated development of AI, avoiding the widening of structural disparities by technological dividends. In his view, although the path of AI development is fraught with uncertainty, one consensus should be formed: clear and steadfast values of "tech for good" must be established for AI, ensuring its development remains responsible to people and society.
